state.misconception_label: Confuses rest and movement on a distance time graph

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: This graph shows how far Fido the dog is from his home. What might the negative-sloping section represent? ![A graph with time (secs) on the horizontal axis and distance (m) on the vertical axis. The graph starts at the origin, travels in a straight line up and right, travels horizontally, then travels in a straight line down and right back to the x-axis. ](). I got Fido has fallen asleep because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: The negative-sloping section of the graph represents Fido moving away from his home, not falling asleep. Remember, on a distance-time graph, a negative slope indicates movement in the opposite direction. Let's focus on why this selected answer is incorrect and discuss the reasoning that leads to the correct interpretation.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Okay, I think I get that the negative slope means Fido is moving back towards home instead of falling asleep. But if he's moving away from home, why does the line go down? Isn't that just showing that he's getting closer to zero distance?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: The negative slope on a distance-time graph does not necessarily mean that Fido is getting closer to zero distance. Remember, a negative slope indicates movement in the opposite direction, not a decrease in distance. Let's focus on understanding how to interpret the direction of movement based on the slope of the graph.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I think I get it a bit better now. So, when the line goes down, it means Fido is moving back towards home, but it doesn't mean he's getting closer to zero distance like I thought. But what if he was just standing still? Would that be a flat line instead?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher makes a critical domain error in Turn 1 (claiming negative slope means moving away when it actually means moving toward home), provides direct answers rather than eliciting reasoning, and while the student does show some improvement by Turn 4 in understanding that downward slope means returning home and flat means stationary, this appears to happen despite rather than because of the teacher's incorrect guidance.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher provides some direct corrective feedback but fails to state explicit procedures or show worked steps for interpreting distance-time graphs, instead offering vague reminders about negative slopes without demonstrating a systematic rule-based approach.
